name: Arrakis world

sections.body:
From the shelter of a sietch, the desert looks like opportunity. There is spice beyond the ridge, room for collectors under the open sky and another settlement somewhere across the sand. The journey between them is where water, equipment and the Maker begin to decide what the colony can afford.

Fremen settlers build around the stone. An Imperial expedition brings a grounded transport and a different body of knowledge. Both must turn finite stores into a living settlement, and both discover that a profitable harvest means little if the people who gathered it cannot return.
sections.title: A home beneath the stone

sections.body:
Deep Erg is exposed dune country with little rock and sparse life. Rocky Basin offers broken stone around sheltered sand, making it natural sietch country. Shield Wall provides escarpments, canyon passages and strong defensive positions.

Deep Desert is high-cost travel through Maker country. It can be crossed but does not permit an ordinary colony or settlement. On local maps, genuine rocky substrate offers worm refuge; a constructed floor laid over sand does not.
sections.title: Erg, basin and shield wall

sections.body:
The recommended opening brings three Fremen survivors with stillsuits, reclamation masks, sandwalking skill and finite supplies. Their knowledge makes desert work possible, while their stores give the colony a limited period to establish collection, food and power.

Choose people who can share construction, growing, cooking, tailoring and hauling. Protect food and install the carried condenser early, then develop windtraps and reclaimed beds without spending the entire construction reserve on expansion.
sections.title: The Fremen sietch start

sections.body:
Six settlers inherit connected chambers cut into the mountain: bunks beneath the rock, places to eat and gather, a kitchen and the beginnings of a workshop. Outside, partly grown pundi rice waits in twenty irrigated beds. Eight windtraps, two cisterns, four sun-cells and three charged batteries give the settlement a head start. The shared reserve holds 120 water rations and 90 packaged meals, with additional water already in the beds and two passive coolers.

The chambers still need hands. Crops need tending, meals need cooking and water must reach each reservoir. Daylight replenishes the batteries; darkness spends them. A nonpolar mountainous site offers a more forgiving first home than a place with prolonged darkness or extreme heat.

This is the Fremen: established mountain sietch start. Its rooms follow the existing mountain rather than replacing it. Where no complete cave layout fits, the arrival choice offers another site or a field-supply opening on the same map without a developed base. Returning to a saved colony never rebuilds lost rooms or renews its starting stores.
sections.title: A sietch already under the mountain

sections.body:
The first harvest changes the question from surviving today to choosing what comes next. A new workshop consumes materials that could have repaired a collector. A spice caravan carries wealth away from the colony before it brings medicine or precision parts home. Growth makes these choices more interesting and their costs harder to ignore.

Everyday care holds the settlement together. Water must reach patients as well as workers. Corpses left near occupied rooms can cause lung rot; a reclamation mask conserves moisture but offers no protection from that illness. The burial ground and the deathstill belong in the settlement’s plans as surely as its pantry.

A raid or fire can undo a comfortable routine. Defenders need to gather rather than meet an attack alone, and firefighters need access to the threatened rooms. Afterward come rescue, treatment and repairs. Reserves give the survivors time to recover before the desert demands another journey.
sections.title: What survives the first season

sections.body:
A visitor brings a history as well as a price. Fremen lives begin among sietch stores and rock shelters; Imperial service produces garrison hands, clerks and assault veterans; towns and spice routes draw their own traders and fighters. These Arrakis biographies accompany the current human roles, including exchange brokers, guards and expedition crew. People already living in an older save keep their histories.

The first Imperial raiding parties may be lightly equipped levies with blades and modest training. Larger forces can afford officers, armored Sardaukar and shield veterans. Among the Fremen are maula scouts, Fedaykin and naibs. Their desert roles avoid shields: a field raised on open sand may attract something more dangerous than the enemy in front of it.
sections.title: People of the desert

sections.body:
House provisioning factors and CHOAM industrial agents maintain reachable trading outposts for supported Fremen colonies. Goodwill, settlement trade and caravan travel govern access. House factors emphasize practical supplies; CHOAM brokers industrial imports and reserved Guild freight.

Guild procurement passes through CHOAM rather than a separate Guild faction. Existing colonies can receive the supported contacts, but a faction that has been destroyed is not brought back.
sections.title: House and CHOAM contacts

sections.body:
A Fremen applicant can ask to join through an accept-or-reject letter. Abandoned freight may offer finite food and materials, while suitable habitat and temperature can bring passing kulon. These opportunities supplement the colony’s work rather than replacing its supply routes.

After a loss, recovery can preserve up to six selected supported Fremen identities, sharing six water rations, four meals and two medicine. Unsupported slots receive a Fremen replacement; without a roster, one survivor is supplied. Emergency assistance adds one Fremen with finite provisions.

Bandit-camp requests require a leader who already shares a supported human enemy with the colony. Broader joiner, resource-pod and wildlife pools remain restricted in the alpha.
sections.title: Visitors, discoveries and recovery

sections.body:
Kulon, Muad’Dib and sand terrapins form the supported native animal roster. Eligible species can appear through migration and self-taming, subject to climate and the usual incident conditions. Kept animals need fodder and physical drinking water; each drink consumes one ration.

An adult female sand terrapin lays an egg about every ten game days, with age and other resource-growth factors affecting the interval. An unfertilized egg provides 0.25 nutrition. With a male, fertilized eggs can hatch after five days at a suitable temperature. This is a slow supplement to food stores.

The supported animals provide no local milk or wool industry. Cloth comes from irrigated fiber and weaving, while specialist textiles are imported.
sections.title: Animals and husbandry

sections.body:
Place sietch meeting markers on genuine worm-safe ground, with a standable approach and no committed Maker hazard. Visitors choose reachable markers; an inaccessible marker does not prevent them from considering another usable one.

A marker directs a visit, not the desert. Ordinary trading duties, pathfinding and active worm hazards still apply, so inspect the route as well as the waiting place.
sections.title: A place for guests to wait

sections.body:
Personal starting possessions are separate from the scenario’s shared stores. In the supported Fremen opening, generated corn becomes Fremen wheat, rice and fungus become pundi rice, and potatoes become Gift to the Thirsty tubers. Physical counts are preserved.

The fungus substitution keeps food value but changes its ingredient and dietary identity. Expanded DLC diets are outside the Core alpha’s supported profile. Existing saved food and unrelated scenarios are not replaced.
sections.title: Personal provisions

sections.body:
The current supported alpha uses RimWorld 1.7.5013 rev95 on Steam’s unstable branch, with Core, Harmony and Sands of Arrakis. Its four openings are Fremen Sietch, Fremen: established mountain sietch, Sardaukar expedition and Sardaukar: stranded patrol. No DLC is required; Geological Landforms and other mod combinations are outside the tested profile.

This Arrakis has working settlements, physical water, spice expeditions, trade, faction research and optional Fremen and Imperial campaign endings. It does not yet offer suspensor flight, worm riding, medical stasis or autonomous faction conquest. The Imperial transport remains grounded.

The alpha is still being balanced and reviewed for ordinary player campaigns and presentation. New colonies and separate backups are the safest way to explore it. The supplied installation, testing and known-issues guides carry the practical release details; the project roadmap records what lies beyond this version.
sections.title: The Arrakis available today

sections.body:
Eleven political actors inhabit a new supported Arrakis world. Fremen sietches, Imperial and House holdings, CHOAM contacts, basin towns and spice-route groups give a journey different destinations and different company. Their settlements have distinct layouts and renewable water for their residents. A town’s stores are not a promise of free water for visitors to your own colony.

Older worlds can opt into this expansion without replacing the factions they already know. Existing inhabited maps receive their water infrastructure once; destruction leaves damage to live with. These are places to visit, trade with or fight, rather than independently simulated empires conquering the planet.
sections.title: Beyond the colony’s doors

summary: A door in the rock, a sealed water store, a trail across the dunes: life on Arrakis grows from small refuges into a place in the struggle for spice.
